cards.description: One number, one verdict. The payoff card almost every video ends on.
A short list laid out as a team sheet, ranked by one metric.
Ranked bars where length encodes magnitude. L12 enforces a visible spread so long names cannot collapse the bars into stubs.
One total taken apart. Parts must sum to the printed total - the renderer refuses to draw otherwise.
Same decomposition as a unit chart. Better when the parts are close in size.
A measured rate against the bar it has to clear. No solver, no residual - the API supplies both numbers.
One row per gameweek, coloured by FDR. Argue from fixtures and you must show the run.
Many entries, little text. Inventory rather than argument.
Whole runs side by side. Comparing clubs' schedules, not one club's week-by-week.
A licensed photo plus the numbers that justify naming him. Photo is CC/PD only on this page — Photo: Bryan Berlin / CC BY-SA 4.0.
How two totals are built, not just which is bigger.
Two players pulling against each other on shared metrics. Minutes sit under the names as the sample the rates were measured over.
Same comparison, columns instead of bars. Reads better when the values are mixed units.
Two faces, no reading required. A scroll-stopper. Photos: Photo: Bryan Berlin / CC BY-SA 4.0; Photo: Bryan Berlin / CC BY-SA 4.0.
Analytical charts from bootstrap-static. Eleven kinds; the generator owns the numbers so a chart cannot contradict the API.
